title: Designing a notification system
idea: A notification system turns domain events into messages over channels, combining Observer, Factory, Strategy and Decorator so new channels plug in without edits.
points: Observer: business code emits `order.shipped` and never calls a channel directly.
Strategy: every channel shares one method, `send(user, text)`.
Factory: one table maps a channel name to the object that serves it.
Decorator: `WithRetry` wraps any channel and adds retries without changing it.

messages.label: emit('order.shipped')
messages.note: The order code announces what happened. It imports nothing about notifications.

messages.label: notify(type, event)
messages.note: The subscribed listener hands the event to the service, which builds the text from a template.

messages.label: push()
messages.note: First use of push: the factory builds a `PushChannel` wrapped in `WithRetry`.

messages.label: channel
messages.note: The service caches the channel and knows only its `send` method.

messages.label: send(user, text)
messages.note: Email has already gone out. The service now calls `send` on the push channel.

messages.label: delivered after retry
messages.note: The inner channel fails once; the decorator retries and returns the delivered line.

code.title: Channels, retry, factory
code.caption: A module of building blocks. `notify.mjs` imports it, so running it alone prints nothing.

walk.text: Strategy: each channel is a class with the same `send(user, text)` method.
`PushChannel` fails on its first call, so the retry has something to do.
Decorator: `WithRetry` has the same `send` and holds the channel it wraps.
It retries until a call succeeds or the tries run out, then rethrows.
Factory: one table names every channel. A new channel adds one line here.

code.title: Wiring it together
code.caption: Three shipped orders for two users. Watch where the retry happens, and where it does not.

walk.text: Each event type has one text builder, kept apart from delivery.
Channels come from the factory on first use and are reused afterwards.
The service loops over the user's preferred channels and calls `send` on each.
Observer: the service subscribes once; the order code only emits.
Order 41 triggers the retry. Order 42 reuses the same push channel.

pitfalls: Keep channel names out of business code; emit events and let preferences decide.
Retry only failures that may pass later; a bad address never succeeds.
`emit` runs listeners synchronously; a channel's thrown error escapes `emit`, so catch inside the listener.

quiz.why: Each `Flaky` succeeds only on its third call. Two tries are not enough, so the first call gives up; three tries reach success.

takeaway: Events in, channels out: each pattern owns one axis of change.
